subject: NanoHealth capacity playbook — follow-up & sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@nanohealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: NanoHealth capacity playbook — follow-up & sizing clarifications

Hi Rita / Paul —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can put together a firm Dedicated proposal and a short comparison to Hosted / Private options.

Recap (from our convo):
- Primary workload: user-facing clinical summarization + patient Q&A (low-latency interactive).
- Peak concurrency observed in pilot: ~220 concurrent user sessions (not all actively generating tokens at once).
- Desired SLA: p95 latency under 350ms for single-turn prompts up to ~1k tokens.
- Data residency: US-only; may evaluate Private VPC if PHI concerns escalate.

Clarifying asks (can you confirm the three below?):
1) Peak sustained TPS (requests/sec) during your busiest 15-minute window?
2) Typical token mix: average input tokens / average output tokens (or a few sample prompt lengths).
3) Are you willing to evaluate 8-bit quantized model variants for cost savings, or do you need FP16 / FP32 for quality?

Preliminary sizing options we plan to model:
A) Cost-optimized Dedicated: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs (mixed batching, KV cache) — target 800–1,200 TPS with warm KV.
B) Latency-optimized Dedicated: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs (lower latency per token, higher single-request throughput) — target 400–600 TPS with p95 latency headroom.
C) Private VPC trial: smaller dedicated pool + Private control plane (compliance lift).

I've attached the initial_capacity_form.xlsx and the call recording for your notes. If you can reply with the three clarifying datapoints above, Ben and I will produce a short playbook with expected TPS/concurrency maps and an initial MAP for procurement.

Next step proposal: 30-minute follow-up Wed to review the playbook. Does Wed 4/7 9:00–9:30 PT work?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: initial_capacity_form.xlsx (spreadsheet), nanohealth_call_recording.mp3 (audio)

From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@nanohealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Chen <p.chen@nanohealth.ai>, procurement <procurement@nanohealth.ai>
Date: 2026-04-02T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NanoHealth capacity playbook — follow-up & sizing clarifications

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below so you can proceed: 

1) Peak sustained TPS: ~450 requests/sec over a 10–15 minute window (this is after we optimized client-side batching). We occasionally spike to ~650rps for <2 minutes during morning syncs.
2) Token mix: average input ~180 tokens; average output ~420 tokens. For heavy clinical draft generation we see inputs ~400 tokens / outputs ~1,200 tokens (rare).
3) Quantization: quality-sensitive tasks (summaries) need FP16 or better for now. We can evaluate quantized variants on lower-criticality endpoints later.

Preference: we are leaning Dedicated for predictable performance; Private VPC if the compliance team flags PHI storage.

We can join Wed 4/7 9:00 PT for a playbook review.

Thanks,
Rita Gomez
Head of Product, NanoHealth
rita.gomez@nanohealth.ai

Note: procurement looped in for licensing/timeline visibility.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@nanohealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: NanoHealth capacity playbook — follow-up & sizing clarifications

Rita / team — good data, thanks. A few micro-technical notes that will shape the final SKU mix: 

- With the token mix you gave (avg 180/420, occasional 400/1200), batching becomes more effective for shorter prompts but you still need single-request latency headroom for the long drafts.
- For the 450 sustained TPS target: two plausible Dedicated configs:
  * 8x A10G-equivalents: best cost/TPS for throughput workloads with aggressive batching and KV reuse. Expect ~600–1,000 sustained TPS depending on batch sizing and sequence lengths.
  * 4x H100-equivalents: fewer GPUs, lower end-to-end latency on single requests and better headroom for the 1200-token outputs; estimated sustained TPS ~350–550.
- Recommendation: start with an 8x-A10G baseline coupled with a small H100 headroom pool for worst-case long-tail latency-sensitive jobs (can be automated via smart routing). This tends to be a good cost/latency trade-off for hybrid mixes.

I've attached a quick scaling calc with sample batch sizes and expected token/sec math (se-scaling-calcs.csv). If you can share a short production trace (1–2 hours of request logs, anonymized), we can run a more precise simulation.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: se-scaling-calcs.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: NanoHealth capacity playbook — follow-up & sizing clarifications

Rita / procurement team —

Following Ben's technical notes, please find a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an initial commercial sketch below. I'll surface a formal commercial in the follow-up but want alignment on timing: 

Mutual Action Plan (high-level):
- 4/2–4/6: Redwood to model two Dedicated configs (8x A10G baseline; 4x H100 alt) and provide estimated TPS, latency p95, and monthly unit costs. (Owner: Ben / Karthik)
- 4/7: Playbook review meeting (30 min) — confirm routing policy and pilot scope. (Owner: Karthik / Rita)
- 4/8–4/15: Pilot provisioning (reserved small pool + canary traffic) + trace capture. (Owner: NanoHealth / Redwood SE)
- 4/20: Pilot readout and procurement decision.

Preliminary commercial sketch (ballpark only):
- 8x A10G baseline: monthly reserved estimate $XXk–$YYk (depends on quantization + support tier).
- 4x H100 alt: premium (~30% higher) for headroom and lower latency.

I'll attach a one-page MAP (MAP_NanoHealth_v1.pdf) that your procurement team can share internally.

Next steps: confirm the 4/7 9:00 PT slot and whether procurement needs a longer lead time for internal approvals.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP_NanoHealth_v1.pdf

Thanks all — appreciate the quick responses and alignment. Wed 4/7 9:00 PT is confirmed on our side. Agenda for the 30-min playbook review:

1) Walkthrough of Ben's simulated TPS/latency trade-offs (8x A10G vs 4x H100).
2) Draft MAP and pilot steps (Marissa).
3) Procurement checklist & timeline (brief) — any gating items?
4) Next rollouts and Private VPC trigger criteria.

Action items for NanoHealth before the meeting:
- Share anonymized 1–2 hour request trace (if available) to tighten simulations.
- Indicate whether PHI will be present in any stored artifacts (this will determine Private VPC requirement).

I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in + agenda and attach Ben's calc + MAP ahead of the call. Looking forward —
